pr_comments:
> Is this a breaking change, because `entity_id` of any existing `utility_meter` sensor with tariffs will change?

It's just a refactor, it will get the same name but now the code is more clean.

The actual change that needs to be done and will break entity_id's is to change in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/69152/files#diff-12949adc26a35f4bf5628940f9ffd274c30435abc9af1b60e5bd39bf76be198fR189

`{meter}` into `{conf_meter_name}` 

But I'm not sure how to proceed without making it breaking. 
I doubt anyone is using `name`, just because it does nothing if you have tariffs, but if it exists it will indeed break the entity_id... 

Ideas ?

To avoid a breaking change, the `utility_meter` can set a suggested `entity_id` based on the slugified equivalent of `f"{meter} {conf_sensor_tariff}"`.
To do that, just set `self.entity_id` in `__init__`, it will be overridden if the requested `entity_id` collides.

issue_context.title: "Entity Not Available" when adding a name to utility_meter
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I had a utility_meter disappear from my dashboard at some point(this month I believe). My main dashboard just says "entity not available" where it was. Nothing in the logs about it. Passes configuration check.

If I remove the "name" from the configuration, it comes back and has all the data there still. I've tried putting the name in quotes, without quotes, with single apostrophes, nothing. It seems like if it has a friendly name at all, it vanishes and doesn't load.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.3.6

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Utility Meter

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/utility_meter/

### Diagnostics information

No logs when it doesn't load

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
utility_meter:
  tesla_energy_month2:
    source: sensor.tesla_wall_charger_kwh
    name: Monthly Tesla Charger Energy
    cycle: monthly
```
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Nothing
```


### Additional information

_No response_
comments:
Hey there @dgomes, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`utility_meter`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L1078) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
Yes but shouldnt the entity id follow the meter identifier not the name. It's rather co fusing to have entity id change just due to adding a friendly name.

> Just because the line "looks" wrong doesn't mean that it is wrong. A quick test shows that adding a name to the config will automatically change the sensor id.
> 
> ```python
> async def test_68508_issue(hass):
>     """Test for issue 68508."""
>     config = {
>         "utility_meter": {
>             "energy_bill": {
>                 "source": "sensor.tesla_wall_charger_kwh",
>                 "cycle": "monthly",
>                 "name": "Monthly Tesla Charger Energy",
>             },
>         }
>     }
> 
>     assert await async_setup_component(hass, DOMAIN, config)
>     assert await async_setup_component(hass, Platform.SENSOR, config)
>     await hass.async_block_till_done()
> 
>     assert not hass.states.get("sensor.energy_bill")
>     assert hass.states.get("sensor.monthly_tesla_charger_energy")
> ```
> 
> Looks normal to me.

Interesting. So your sensor actually loads for you? I’ll turn on debug logging and see what I can find. My sensor doesn’t load as soon as I add a name as I did above, but it passes the config check.

> Yes but shouldnt the entity id follow the meter identifier not the name. It's rather co fusing to have entity id change just due to adding a friendly name.

Possibly, but I just don't think it's linked to #63808, which is why I commented.

> Interesting. So your sensor actually loads for you? I’ll turn on debug logging and see what I can find. My sensor doesn’t load as soon as I add a name as I did above, but it passes the config check.

I don't have any sensors - I don't use the integration. I just built a Unit Test to check the behavior.
It seems to me the behaviour here has always been as it is now.

> Yes but shouldnt the entity id follow the meter identifier not the name. It's rather co fusing to have entity id change just due to adding a friendly name.

Extra note on this one: it seems that if tariffs are defined, then the behaviour is different.
- with tariffs: `CONF_NAME: f"{meter} {tariff}"`
- without tariffs: `CONF_NAME: conf.get(CONF_NAME, meter)`

I am guessing that splitting out the `entity id` and the `friendly name` would be a breaking change for all users which have already set a name and don't use tariffs.

Maybe it should be something like this:
- with tariffs: `CONF_ID: f"{meter} {tariff}"`, `CONF_NAME: f"{conf.get(CONF_NAME, meter)} {tariff}"`
- without tariffs: `CONF_ID: meter`, `CONF_NAME: conf.get(CONF_NAME, meter)`

with all this discussion I realised that the use of name to set a friendly name is an outdated pattern in HA, we are better off using unique_id and leave the user the chance to rename the utility_meter sensor to whatever he prefers
